title: Festivals & Celebrations (节日与庆祝)
description: Talk about Chinese festivals — Spring Festival, Mid-Autumn Festival and Dragon Boat Festival — their foods and customs, celebrate birthdays, discuss holidays and travel, and learn festival dos and don'ts.

notes.heading: 🧧 Spring Festival (春节 chūnjié)
notes.body:
春节 **chūnjié** (Spring Festival), also called 中国新年 (Chinese New Year), is the most important festival in China.

Key customs:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 春节 | chūnjié | Spring Festival / Chinese New Year |
| 过年 | guònián | to celebrate the New Year |
| 红包 | hóngbāo | red envelope (with lucky money) |
| 饺子 | jiǎozi | dumplings (the classic festival food) |
| 烟花 | yānhuā | fireworks |
| 新年快乐 | xīnnián kuàilè | Happy New Year |

💡 **Worked Example:** 过年的时候，孩子拿红包。Guònián de shíhou, háizi ná hóngbāo. — At New Year, children receive red envelopes. (…的时候 = when/at the time of…)

📎 **Key Points:**
- Families gather for a big dinner on New Year's Eve; dumplings symbolise wealth.
- Red is everywhere — it scares away bad luck.
- Greet people with 新年快乐！Xīnnián kuàilè!

notes.heading: 🌕 Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节)
notes.body:
中秋节 **zhōngqiūjié** (Mid-Autumn Festival) is the festival of the full moon and family reunion, in the eighth lunar month.

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 中秋节 | zhōngqiūjié | Mid-Autumn Festival |
| 月饼 | yuèbǐng | mooncake |
| 月亮 | yuèliang | the moon |
| 赏月 | shǎng yuè | to admire the moon |
| 团圆 | tuányuán | to reunite (family) |

💡 **Worked Example:** 中秋节我们吃月饼、赏月。Zhōngqiūjié wǒmen chī yuèbǐng, shǎng yuè. — At Mid-Autumn Festival we eat mooncakes and admire the moon.

🔑 **How it works:** 月 **yuè** means 'moon' — you can see it in both 月饼 (moon-cake) and 月亮 (the moon). The round moon and round mooncakes symbolise family reunion (团圆).

notes.heading: 🐉 Dragon Boat Festival (端午节)
notes.body:
端午节 **duānwǔjié** (Dragon Boat Festival) falls in the fifth lunar month and honours the ancient poet Qu Yuan.

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 端午节 | duānwǔjié | Dragon Boat Festival |
| 粽子 | zòngzi | sticky rice dumplings wrapped in leaves |
| 龙舟 | lóngzhōu | dragon boat |
| 比赛 | bǐsài | race / competition |

💡 **Worked Example:** 端午节人们吃粽子，看龙舟比赛。Duānwǔjié rénmen chī zòngzi, kàn lóngzhōu bǐsài. — At Dragon Boat Festival people eat zongzi and watch dragon boat races.

📎 **Key Points:**
- 龙 **lóng** = dragon, 舟 **zhōu** = boat — 龙舟 is literally 'dragon boat'.
- People race dragon boats and eat 粽子 to remember the poet Qu Yuan, who drowned himself in a river; legend says food was thrown into the water so fish would not harm him.
- 人们 **rénmen** = people (in general).

notes.heading: 🎂 Birthdays (生日 shēngrì)
notes.body:
生日 **shēngrì** means birthday. Key phrases:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 生日快乐 | shēngrì kuàilè | happy birthday |
| 生日蛋糕 | shēngrì dàngāo | birthday cake |
| 礼物 | lǐwù | gift |
| 生日会 | shēngrì huì | birthday party |

💡 **Worked Example:**
A: 明天是我的生日。Míngtiān shì wǒ de shēngrì. — Tomorrow is my birthday.
B: 生日快乐！祝你生日快乐！Shēngrì kuàilè! Zhù nǐ shēngrì kuàilè! — Happy birthday! (祝 **zhù** = to wish)

🔑 **How it works:** 快乐 **kuàilè** = happy — combine it with any celebration: 生日快乐 (happy birthday), 新年快乐 (happy new year).

📎 **Key Points:**
- Ask someone's age with 你几岁了？(children) or 你多大了？(older): 你今年几岁了？Nǐ jīnnián jǐ suì le? — How old are you this year?
- Traditionally, long noodles (长寿面 'long-life noodles') are eaten on birthdays for long life.

notes.heading: 🏖️ Holidays & Travel (假期 jiàqī)
notes.body:
| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 假期 | jiàqī | holiday / vacation |
| 放假 | fàngjià | to have a holiday (school/work closes) |
| 旅行 | lǚxíng | to travel |
| 旅游 | lǚyóu | to tour / travel for fun |
| 坐飞机 | zuò fēijī | to take a plane |
| 坐火车 | zuò huǒchē | to take a train |

💡 **Worked Example:**
A: 假期你去哪儿了？Jiàqī nǐ qù nǎr le? — Where did you go in the holiday?
B: 我去北京旅行了。Wǒ qù Běijīng lǚxíng le. — I travelled to Beijing.

🔑 **How it works:** 坐 **zuò** (to sit/ride) + vehicle = to travel by that vehicle: 坐火车 (by train), 坐飞机 (by plane).

📎 **Key Point:** 了 after the verb marks a completed action: 我去了 (I went).

notes.heading: 🧭 Festival Dos and Don'ts
notes.body:
Festival customs carry meaning — some things are lucky, others taboo.

**Lucky:**
- Wear red and use red decorations at New Year — red drives away bad luck.
- Give 红包 with lucky money; the number 8 (八 bā) is lucky because it sounds like 发 **fā** (to prosper).
- Say 新年快乐 and 恭喜发财 **gōngxǐ fācái** (wishing you prosperity).

**Taboos:**
- Don't give a clock (送钟 sòng zhōng) — it sounds like attending a funeral.
- Don't give pears (梨 lí) to couples — it sounds like 离 (to separate).
- Avoid sweeping or breaking things on New Year's Day — you might sweep or break your luck away.

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** when giving or receiving a red envelope or gift, use **both hands** — one hand looks casual or rude.

✅ **Check:** which gift would be a bad idea for a Chinese friend, a clock or mooncakes? (Answer: the clock.)

notes.heading: 🗣️ Talking About Festivals: Useful Patterns
notes.body:
Combine festival vocabulary with patterns you know:

- **…的时候** (at the time of…): 春节的时候，我们吃饺子。At Spring Festival we eat dumplings.
- **会 huì** (will / can): 你会收到红包。Nǐ huì shōudào hóngbāo. — You will receive red envelopes.
- **可以 kěyǐ** (may / can): 假期我们可以去旅行。Jiàqī wǒmen kěyǐ qù lǚxíng. — In the holidays we can travel.
- **最喜欢** (like most): 我最喜欢中秋节。Wǒ zuì xǐhuan zhōngqiūjié. — I like Mid-Autumn Festival best. (最 **zuì** = most)

💡 **Worked Example:**
A: 你最喜欢什么节日？Nǐ zuì xǐhuan shénme jiérì? — Which festival do you like best?
B: 我最喜欢春节，因为可以拿红包。Wǒ zuì xǐhuan chūnjié, yīnwèi kěyǐ ná hóngbāo. — I like Spring Festival best, because we get red envelopes.

🔑 **How it works:** 最 + adjective/verb makes the superlative: 最好 (best), 最喜欢 (like most), 最大 (biggest). 节日 **jiérì** is the general word for 'festival'.

flashcards.definition: Spring Festival — Chinese New Year, the most important festival in China.
flashcards.example: 春节我们吃饺子。Chūnjié wǒmen chī jiǎozi. (At Spring Festival we eat dumplings.)

flashcards.definition: Red envelope with lucky money, given at New Year and weddings.
flashcards.example: 过年的时候，孩子拿红包。Guònián de shíhou, háizi ná hóngbāo. (At New Year, children get red envelopes.)

flashcards.definition: Mid-Autumn Festival — the festival of the full moon and family reunion.
flashcards.example: 中秋节我们赏月。Zhōngqiūjié wǒmen shǎng yuè. (At Mid-Autumn Festival we admire the moon.)

flashcards.definition: Mooncake — the round festival cake eaten at Mid-Autumn Festival.
flashcards.example: 月饼很好吃。Yuèbǐng hěn hǎochī. (Mooncakes are delicious.)

flashcards.definition: Dragon Boat Festival — honours the poet Qu Yuan with boat races and zongzi.
flashcards.example: 端午节有龙舟比赛。Duānwǔjié yǒu lóngzhōu bǐsài. (There are dragon boat races at the festival.)

flashcards.definition: Sticky rice dumplings wrapped in leaves, eaten at Dragon Boat Festival.
flashcards.example: 端午节人们吃粽子。Duānwǔjié rénmen chī zòngzi. (People eat zongzi at Dragon Boat Festival.)

flashcards.definition: Happy birthday. 快乐 (happy) combines with any celebration.
flashcards.example: 祝你生日快乐！Zhù nǐ shēngrì kuàilè! (Happy birthday to you!)

flashcards.definition: Holiday / vacation. 放假 = to have time off.
flashcards.example: 假期我们去旅行。Jiàqī wǒmen qù lǚxíng. (We travel in the holidays.)

flashcards.definition: To travel. 去旅游 = to travel for fun.
flashcards.example: 我去北京旅行了。Wǒ qù Běijīng lǚxíng le. (I travelled to Beijing.)

flashcards.definition: To take a plane. 坐 + vehicle = to travel by it: 坐火车 (by train).
flashcards.example: 我们坐飞机去上海。Wǒmen zuò fēijī qù Shànghǎi. (We fly to Shanghai.)

flashcards.definition: Happy New Year — the key Spring Festival greeting.
flashcards.example: 新年快乐！恭喜发财！Xīnnián kuàilè! Gōngxǐ fācái! (Happy New Year! Wishing you prosperity!)

flashcards.definition: Most — makes the superlative: 最喜欢 (like best), 最大 (biggest).
flashcards.example: 我最喜欢春节。Wǒ zuì xǐhuan chūnjié. (I like Spring Festival best.)

questions.explanation: 春节 chūnjié is Spring Festival, another name for Chinese New Year — the most important festival in China.
月饼 are mooncakes — 月 means moon — eaten at Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节), the festival of the full moon.
生日 means birthday and 快乐 means happy, so 生日快乐 is 'happy birthday'. New Year uses 新年快乐.

choices: Sticky rice dumplings wrapped in leaves
questions.explanation: 粽子 are sticky rice dumplings wrapped in bamboo leaves, the traditional food of the Dragon Boat Festival.
假期 jiàqī means holiday or vacation: 假期你去哪儿了？(Where did you go in the holiday?)

questions.stem: What do children traditionally receive at Spring Festival?
questions.explanation: Children receive 红包 — red envelopes containing lucky money. Clocks are a taboo gift and mooncakes belong to Mid-Autumn.

questions.stem: 端午节人们吃粽子，看龙舟比赛。(Duānwǔjié rénmen chī zòngzi, kàn lóngzhōu bǐsài.) What do people do at this festival?
choices: Eat mooncakes and watch the moon
Eat zongzi and watch dragon boat races
Give red envelopes and light fireworks
Eat birthday cake and sing songs
questions.explanation: The sentence says people eat zongzi (粽子) and watch dragon boat races (龙舟比赛) — the two Dragon Boat Festival customs.

questions.stem: 我们坐飞机去上海。(Wǒmen zuò fēijī qù Shànghǎi.) How do they travel?
questions.explanation: 坐 + vehicle means 'to travel by': 飞机 is a plane, so 坐飞机 = to fly. A train would be 火车.

questions.stem: Why is giving a clock (送钟) a taboo gift in Chinese culture?
choices: It sounds like the words for attending a funeral
It means the friendship will grow
questions.explanation: 送钟 (sòng zhōng, to give a clock) sounds like the phrase for attending a funeral, making clocks an unlucky gift.

questions.stem: 我最喜欢中秋节。(Wǒ zuì xǐhuan zhōngqiūjié.) means:
questions.explanation: 最 makes the superlative: 最喜欢 = like most/best, so the speaker's favourite festival is Mid-Autumn Festival.

questions.stem: 春节的时候，我们吃饺子。(Chūnjié de shíhou, wǒmen chī jiǎozi.) What does …的时候 mean?
questions.explanation: …的时候 means 'when/at the time of…': 春节的时候 = at Spring Festival time, so the family eats dumplings then.

questions.stem: The number 8 (八 bā) is considered lucky in Chinese culture because:
choices: It sounds like the word for prosper (发 fā)
It is the number of festivals
questions.explanation: 八 bā sounds close to 发 fā (to prosper/get rich), so 8 appears in lucky money amounts and phone numbers.

questions.stem: A: 你最喜欢什么节日？B: 我最喜欢春节，因为可以拿红包。Why does B like Spring Festival best?
choices: Because they can receive red envelopes
questions.explanation: 因为可以拿红包 means 'because (I) can get red envelopes' — 因为 gives the reason after stating the favourite festival.

questions.stem: Which pairing of festival and food is correct?
choices: 端午节 — 月饼 (Dragon Boat Festival — mooncakes)
中秋节 — 粽子 (Mid-Autumn Festival — zongzi)
春节 — 月饼 (Spring Festival — mooncakes)
中秋节 — 月饼 (Mid-Autumn Festival — mooncakes)
questions.explanation: Mooncakes belong to Mid-Autumn Festival; zongzi belong to Dragon Boat Festival and dumplings to Spring Festival.

questions.stem: A friend says: 假期我去北京旅行了。我们坐火车去的。(Jiàqī wǒ qù Běijīng lǚxíng le. Wǒmen zuò huǒchē qù de.) What do we learn?
choices: They will fly to Beijing next holiday
They travelled to Beijing in the holiday, going by train
They live in Beijing and never travel
They travelled to Beijing by plane
questions.explanation: 了 marks a completed trip: 去旅行了 = travelled, and 坐火车去的 = went by train — a past holiday trip by rail, not a future flight.
